cards.hypothesis: Subjects with blunted cortisol reactivity exhibit systematically lower EDA phasic amplitude during stress, causing Mondrian's EDA-based taxonomy bins to misclassify their stress windows as baseline-like, yielding prediction intervals that are too narrow.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Blunted HPA-axis reactivity -> reduced sudomotor activation -> lower EDA phasic driver amplitude -> assignment to low-arousal Mondrian bin -> conformal quantile calibrated on predominantly baseline-like windows -> undercoverage for true stress windows.
cards.causal_path: cortisol_reactivity (AUCg) -> EDA_phasic_amplitude (cvxEDA driver) -> mondrian_bin_assignment -> conformal_quantile_width -> coverage_indicator
control_variables: stratify by cortisol_reactivity_tertile; include baseline_EDA_tonic as covariate in quantile regression; restrict to medication-free subjects
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage stems from random label noise in stress condition annotations, not physiological phenotype.
cards.rival_prediction: Undercoverage correlates with annotation disagreement metrics but not with cortisol_reactivity_AUCg.
cards.distinguishing_test: Fit logistic regression: undercoverage_indicator ~ cortisol_reactivity_AUCg + annotation_disagreement_score. H1 predicts significant cortisol coefficient (p<0.05) after controlling for annotation_disagreement; rival predicts only annotation_disagreement significant.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Prior WESAD analyses show cortisol_reactivity explains ~15% variance in EDA stress response; Mondrian bin misassignment amplifies this to coverage deficits.
minimum_data_needed: subject-level cortisol AUCg from saliva samples
continuous EDA at 700Hz from chest sensor
Mondrian taxonomy bin assignments per window
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects in lowest cortisol_reactivity tertile show empirical coverage at least 10 percentage points below nominal 90% level, while highest tertile achieves nominal coverage.
cards.failure_condition: No significant difference in empirical coverage across cortisol_reactivity tertiles (ANOVA p>0.05) after controlling for baseline_EDA_tonic.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Two-way ANOVA: empirical_coverage ~ cortisol_tertile * mondrian_bin, with baseline_EDA_tonic as covariate. Post-hoc Tukey HSD for tertile contrasts. Alpha=0.05.
cards.falsification_test: Re-run Mondrian with cortisol_reactivity as explicit taxonomy feature. If undercoverage persists for low-cortisol subjects despite correct bin assignment, H1 mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Wrist-worn ACC magnitude exceeds 0.5g for >30% of stress windows in specific subjects due to idiosyncratic motor behaviors (e.g., fidgeting, gesturing), inducing motion artifacts in wrist EDA/TEMP that distort Mondrian's wrist-sensor taxonomy bins.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Idiosyncratic motor behavior -> high wrist ACC magnitude -> motion artifact contamination of wrist EDA/TEMP -> shifted feature distribution in wrist-sensor Mondrian bins -> conformal quantiles calibrated on artifact-contaminated windows -> undercoverage for clean stress windows.
control_variables: include chest_ACC_magnitude as covariate; restrict analysis to non-dominant wrist; normalize by subject-specific ACC baseline
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage arises from chest sensor signal quality differences, not wrist motion artifacts.
cards.rival_prediction: Undercoverage correlates with chest_EDA_noise_index but not with wrist_ACC_magnitude_95th.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compute partial correlation: coverage ~ wrist_ACC_magnitude_95th | chest_EDA_noise_index. H1 predicts significant negative partial correlation (p<0.05); rival predicts non-significant.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Motion artifacts can shift EDA features by >2 SD; Mondrian bins are sensitive to feature distribution shifts; prior work shows >20% coverage drop under artifact contamination.
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with wrist_ACC_magnitude_95th > 0.5g show empirical coverage <80% at nominal 90%; subjects below threshold achieve >88% coverage.
cards.failure_condition: No significant coverage difference between high-ACC and low-ACC subjects (t-test p>0.05) after controlling for chest_ACC_magnitude.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed model: empirical_coverage ~ wrist_ACC_magnitude_95th + chest_ACC_magnitude + (1|subject). Test wrist_ACC coefficient <0 at alpha=0.05.
cards.falsification_test: Apply artifact removal (wavelet denoising + ACC regression) to wrist EDA/TEMP before Mondrian binning. If undercoverage persists for high-ACC subjects, H2 is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Non-stationary EDA phasic response dynamics within the stress condition (habituation/sensitization) cause early stress windows to populate different Mondrian bins than late windows, but conformal calibration pools them, yielding miscalibrated quantiles for late windows in sensitizing subjects.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Within-stress temporal dynamics -> EDA_phasic_amplitude trend (habituation/sensitization) -> time-dependent Mondrian bin assignment -> pooled conformal calibration ignores temporal structure -> quantiles miscalibrated for late windows in sensitizing subjects -> undercoverage.
control_variables: include baseline_EDA as covariate; counterbalance condition order; restrict to first stress exposure per subject
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is constant across stress windows; temporal dynamics are irrelevant.
cards.rival_prediction: Empirical coverage does not vary significantly with stress_window_index (slope ~0).
cards.distinguishing_test: Fit linear model: coverage_indicator ~ stress_window_index * sensitization_group (slope>0 vs slope<0). H1 predicts significant interaction (p<0.05); rival predicts no interaction.
cards.effect_size_rationale: EDA habituation slopes of -0.1 to -0.3 µS/window documented in WESAD; Mondrian bin transitions amplify this to ~5-15% coverage drift across 10 windows.
cards.testable_prediction: For sensitizing subjects (positive EDA slope), coverage in last 3 stress windows is >15pp lower than in first 3 windows; for habituating subjects, coverage is stable or higher in late windows.
cards.failure_condition: No significant coverage difference between early and late stress windows for any sensitization group (paired t-test p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Mixed-effects logistic regression: coverage_binary ~ window_index * sensitization_group + (1|subject). Test interaction term at alpha=0.05.
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate conformal predictors separately for early (windows 1-3) and late (windows 8-10) stress windows. If late-window calibration achieves nominal coverage for sensitizing subjects, H3 mechanism (pooled calibration) is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Self-reported stress labels (VAS) for certain subjects show high intra-subject variability (CV>0.4) during the stress condition, indicating ambiguous labeling that contaminates Mondrian's label-conditional calibration sets.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Ambiguous self-report -> high VAS variability within stress condition -> label noise in calibration set -> Mondrian's label-conditional conformal quantiles inflated by mislabeled baseline-like windows -> undercoverage for truly stressed windows.
control_variables: exclude subjects with VAS_compliance<80%; include alexithymia_score as covariate; use only chest-sensor features for binning to avoid label leakage
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage stems from physiological non-response, not label noise.
cards.rival_prediction: Undercoverage correlates with physiological non-response markers (e.g., low EDA reactivity) but not with VAS_stress_CV.
cards.distinguishing_test: Structural equation model: coverage ~ VAS_stress_CV + EDA_reactivity. H1 predicts direct effect of VAS_CV on coverage (p<0.05) controlling for EDA_reactivity; rival predicts only EDA_reactivity significant.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Label noise typically causes modest coverage deficits (3-8pp) unless noise >30%; WESAD VAS CV>0.4 occurs in ~20% of subjects.
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with VAS_stress_CV > 0.4 show empirical coverage 5-10pp below nominal; subjects with CV < 0.2 achieve nominal coverage.
cards.failure_condition: No significant correlation between VAS_stress_CV and empirical coverage (Spearman rho p>0.05) after controlling for EDA_reactivity.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Partial Spearman correlation: coverage vs VAS_CV controlling for EDA_reactivity. Bootstrap 95% CI for partial rho. Reject if CI excludes 0.
cards.falsification_test: Replace VAS labels with physiological stress labels (unsupervised clustering of chest EDA/ECG/RESP). If undercoverage persists for high-VAS-CV subjects under physiological labels, H4 is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Mondrian's fixed taxonomy (based on marginal feature quantiles) creates bins with highly imbalanced subject representation; rare-subject bins have <20 calibration points, yielding unstable conformal quantiles that undercover for those subjects.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Inter-subject feature variability -> skewed Mondrian bin population -> sparse calibration sets for rare-subject bins -> high variance in conformal quantile estimation -> systematic undercoverage for subjects in sparse bins.
control_variables: use subject-stratified binning; minimum bin size threshold; adaptive taxonomy depth
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to feature distribution shift between calibration and test, not bin sparsity.
cards.rival_prediction: Undercoverage correlates with calibration-test distribution distance (e.g., MMD) but not with bin_calibration_count.
cards.distinguishing_test: Regression: coverage ~ bin_calibration_count + MMD_calibration_test. H1 predicts significant bin_count coefficient (p<0.05) controlling for MMD; rival predicts only MMD significant.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Conformal theory: quantile variance ~ 1/(n+1); bins with n<20 have >15% quantile CV; WESAD has 15 subjects, 10 bins -> several bins inevitably sparse.
minimum_data_needed: Mondrian bin assignments for all calibration windows
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects whose stress windows fall in bins with calibration_count < 20 show coverage <80%; subjects in bins with count > 50 achieve >88% coverage.
cards.failure_condition: No significant coverage difference between sparse-bin and dense-bin subjects (t-test p>0.05) after controlling for MMD.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Weighted least squares: empirical_coverage ~ bin_calibration_count + MMD, weights = bin_count. Test bin_count coefficient >0 at alpha=0.05.
cards.falsification_test: Re-run Mondrian with minimum bin size = 30 (merging sparse bins). If undercoverage disappears for previously sparse-bin subjects, H5 is confirmed; if it persists, H5 is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Chest RESP signal exhibits subject-specific baseline wander (0.05-0.15 Hz) during stress due to sighing/deep breathing, distorting RESP-derived features (rate, variability) used in Mondrian taxonomy, causing systematic bin misassignment for sigh-prone subjects.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Sighing behavior -> RESP baseline wander -> corrupted RESP_rate and RESP_RV features -> incorrect Mondrian bin assignment -> conformal quantiles from wrong physiological regime -> undercoverage.
cards.causal_path: sigh_rate_per_minute -> RESP_baseline_wander_amplitude -> RESP_feature_distortion -> mondrian_bin_misassignment -> conformal_quantile_error -> coverage_deficit
control_variables: include overall_respiratory_rate as covariate; use chest_strap_tightness_log; restrict to seated posture
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage for these subjects is due to ECG-derived HRV artifacts from respiration, not RESP feature distortion.
cards.rival_prediction: Undercoverage correlates with HRV_artifact_index but not with RESP_baseline_wander_RMS.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare two Mondrian models: (A) with RESP features, (B) without RESP features. H1 predicts coverage improves for high-sigh subjects in model B; rival predicts no change.
cards.effect_size_rationale: RESP baseline wander can shift rate estimates by 3-5 breaths/min; Mondrian bins on rate quantiles; misassignment rate ~30% for high-sigh subjects -> 10-15pp coverage drop.
minimum_data_needed: sigh annotations or automated sigh detection
Mondrian bin assignments with/without RESP features
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with sigh_rate > 3/min show >10pp coverage improvement when RESP features excluded from Mondrian taxonomy; low-sigh subjects show <2pp change.
cards.failure_condition: No significant coverage difference between RESP-included and RESP-excluded models for high-sigh subjects (paired t-test p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Paired t-test: coverage_with_RESP vs coverage_without_RESP for high-sigh subjects. Alpha=0.05. Effect size: Cohen's d.
cards.falsification_test: Apply high-pass filter (0.15Hz) to RESP before feature extraction. If undercoverage persists for high-sigh subjects, H6 is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Sensor calibration drift in wrist TEMP (thermistor) over the 60-minute protocol causes systematic temperature underestimation in later conditions, shifting late-stress windows into cooler Mondrian bins with narrower conformal quantiles.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Thermistor self-heating / ambient drift -> wrist_TEMP_bias increasing over time -> late stress windows assigned to low-TEMP Mondrian bins -> conformal quantiles calibrated on cooler (baseline/amusement) windows -> undercoverage for late stress.
control_variables: monitor ambient temperature; include condition_order as factor; use chest TEMP as reference
cards.rival_explanation: Temporal coverage drop is due to physiological habituation, not sensor drift.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage drops similarly for chest TEMP (which has no drift) if habituation is the cause.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage drift for wrist TEMP vs chest TEMP across protocol time. H1 predicts wrist-specific drift; rival predicts parallel drift.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Thermistor drift ~0.1-0.3°C over 60min; Mondrian TEMP bins ~0.5°C wide; ~20% of late windows misbinned -> 3-6pp coverage drop.
cards.testable_prediction: Wrist TEMP shows negative bias trend >0.15°C over protocol; coverage for stress condition drops >5pp from first to last stress block; chest TEMP shows no bias trend and no coverage drop.
cards.failure_condition: No significant wrist TEMP bias trend (linear regression slope p>0.05) OR coverage drop not wrist-specific (chest TEMP shows similar drop).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear regression: wrist_TEMP_bias ~ elapsed_time. Mixed model: coverage ~ elapsed_time * sensor_location (wrist/chest) + (1|subject). Test interaction at alpha=0.05.
cards.falsification_test: Apply post-hoc drift correction to wrist TEMP (linear detrending per subject). If coverage drop persists after correction, H7 is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Residual physiological arousal from the preceding amusement condition contaminates the stress baseline for subjects with slow EDA recovery (tau>30s), causing their early stress windows to be binned as high-arousal but conformal quantiles reflect true stress distribution, yielding overcoverage early and undercoverage late.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Slow EDA recovery from amusement -> elevated tonic EDA at stress onset -> early stress windows assigned to high-arousal Mondrian bins -> conformal quantiles too wide for early windows -> quantiles too narrow for late windows after recovery -> undercoverage in late stress.
control_variables: standardize inter_condition_interval; include amusement_intensity rating; control for baseline_EDA
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage variation across stress windows is due to within-stress habituation (H3), not prior-condition contamination.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage pattern correlates with within-stress EDA slope, not with amusement_recovery_tau.
cards.distinguishing_test: Multiple regression: coverage_window_10 ~ within_stress_EDA_slope + amusement_recovery_tau. H1 predicts significant amusement_recovery_tau coefficient (p<0.05) controlling for within_stress_slope; rival predicts only within_stress_slope significant.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Slow recovery (tau>30s) affects ~25% of subjects; can elevate tonic EDA by 0.5-1µS at stress onset; Mondrian bins shift by 1-2 levels -> 10-15pp coverage swing across stress windows.
cards.testable_prediction: Subjects with amusement_recovery_tau > 30s show coverage_window_1 > 95% and coverage_window_10 < 80%; fast-recovery subjects show stable coverage ~90%.
cards.failure_condition: No significant correlation between amusement_recovery_tau and (coverage_window_1 - coverage_window_10) (Spearman p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Spearman correlation: amusement_recovery_tau vs coverage_drop (window_1 - window_10). Bootstrap 95% CI. Alpha=0.05.
cards.falsification_test: Insert 5-min rest between amusement and stress. If coverage pattern disappears, H8 confirmed; if persists, H8 falsified (supports H3).

cards.hypothesis: Subjects with high resting heart rate variability (RMSSD>50ms) exhibit paradoxical HRV increase during stress (vagal withdrawal failure), causing their stress windows to fall into Mondrian bins dominated by baseline/amusement windows, yielding over-wide conformal quantiles that nevertheless undercover due to bimodal score distribution.
cards.proposed_mechanism: High baseline RMSSD -> blunted HRV stress response (or paradoxical increase) -> stress HRV features overlap baseline distribution -> Mondrian bin mixes stress and baseline -> conformal scores bimodal -> quantile covers modes but misses anti-modes -> undercoverage.
control_variables: restrict to medication-free; control breathing_rate via RESP; include fitness_proxy (resting_HR)
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage for high-RMSSD subjects is due to EDA non-response, not HRV paradoxical response.
cards.rival_prediction: Undercoverage correlates with EDA_reactivity but not with stress_HRV_change_RMSSD.
cards.distinguishing_test: Stratify by baseline_RMSSD tertile. Within high-RMSSD tertile, compare coverage for paradoxical-HRV (stress_RMSSD > baseline) vs normal-HRV responders. H1 predicts lower coverage for paradoxical subgroup; rival predicts no difference.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Paradoxical HRV response prevalence unknown in WESAD; need to estimate proportion with stress_RMSSD > baseline_RMSSD and their coverage deficit. Pilot analysis of 5 subjects would estimate effect size.
minimum_data_needed: baseline and stress RMSSD per subject
cards.testable_prediction: High-RMSSD subjects with paradoxical HRV response show coverage <80%; high-RMSSD normal responders show coverage >88%.
cards.failure_condition: No coverage difference between paradoxical and normal HRV responders within high-RMSSD tertile (t-test p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Within high-RMSSD tertile: t-test coverage_paradoxical vs coverage_normal. Alpha=0.05. Report Cohen's d.
cards.falsification_test: Re-run Mondrian with HRV features excluded. If undercoverage persists for paradoxical-HRV subjects, H9 is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Mondrian's exchangeability assumption is violated for subjects with circadian-phase-dependent stress reactivity (e.g., evening types tested in morning), causing systematic conformal score distribution shift between calibration (mixed chronotypes) and test (specific chronotype) that manifests as undercoverage.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Chronotype x time-of-day interaction -> stress_reactivity_phenotype -> feature_distribution_shift -> conformal_score_distribution_shift -> quantile_miscalibration -> undercoverage for misaligned chronotypes.
cards.causal_path: chronotype_score * test_time_of_day -> stress_EDA_ECG_feature_vector -> mondrian_bin_assignment -> conformal_score_cdf -> coverage_indicator
control_variables: include sleep_duration and caffeine as covariates; restrict to regular sleepers; balance time-of-day across chronotypes in calibration
cards.rival_explanation: Undercoverage is due to general inter-subject variability, not chronotype-time interaction.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage correlates with overall feature distance to calibration mean, not with chronotype*time interaction.
cards.distinguishing_test: Fit model: coverage ~ chronotype*time_of_day + feature_distance_to_calibration_mean. H1 predicts significant interaction (p<0.05) controlling for feature_distance; rival predicts only feature_distance significant.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Circadian effects on stress reactivity ~5-10% variance; Mondrian bins may partially absorb; expected coverage deficit 3-8pp for misaligned subjects.
cards.testable_prediction: Evening types tested before 10am show coverage <85%; morning types tested before 10am show coverage >88%. Evening types tested after 2pm show coverage >88%.
cards.failure_condition: No significant chronotype*time_of_day interaction on coverage (linear model p>0.05) after controlling for feature_distance.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear model: coverage ~ chronotype * time_of_day_block + feature_distance + sleep_duration + caffeine. Test interaction at alpha=0.05.
cards.falsification_test: Re-calibrate Mondrian separately for each chronotype*time_of_day block. If undercoverage disappears, H10 confirmed; if persists, H10 falsified (shift not captured by taxonomy).
